senate: Class 3 (34 seats) is up in 2028, Class 2 (33) in 2032 and Class 1 (33) in 2036. The counts match the task brief.

The Florida and Ohio Class 3 seats are filled by appointees (Moody, Husted) until the November 3, 2026 special elections; those specials cover the unexpired terms ending January 3, 2029, so both seats have their regular full-term election in 2028 as part of Class 3. They are not extra 2028 seats.
Special elections for seats vacated after this inventory was written are out of scope; add them when they are called, as the brief says.

Vermont has no Class 2 seat and Nebraska/Alaska have no Class 3 / Class 1 seat respectively, so the 'Another party or independent' exceptions in SEEDS.md apply only to the cycles in which those states actually vote.
governors: The brief expected 11 presidential-year governor races; confirmed: DE, IN, MO, MT, NH, NC, ND, UT, VT, WA, WV.
Puerto Rico and American Samoa also elect governors in presidential years; territories are out of scope.
Incumbents are as of 2026-10-06 and informational only. NH and VT hold elections on 2026-11-03, so their 2028 incumbents are unknown.

Vermont: Vt. Const. ch. II, § 47 — if no candidate has a majority, the General Assembly elects the governor from the top three by joint ballot in January. The market resolves to the party of whoever is finally elected by that process.
Washington: top-two general election (two candidates advance from the August primary; the general is decided by plurality of the two).
No presidential-year governor race has a general-election runoff.
president: Counts: 51 statewide units + 5 district units + 1 national = 57 markets per cycle, as the brief expected.

2028 uses the 2020-census apportionment (538 electors). 2032 and 2036 use the 2030-census apportionment: state elector counts will change and Maine or Nebraska could gain or lose a district. A district that no longer exists resolves N/A; the statewide markets are unaffected.

Nebraska: a winner-take-all constitutional amendment was pushed by initiative petition for the 2026 ballot and by LR24CA in the Legislature (which failed). If Nebraska stops awarding electors by district before an election, the NE-1/2/3 markets for that election resolve N/A.
Maine awards electors by district under 21-A M.R.S. § 802; ranked-choice tabulation applies to presidential electors in Maine (since 2020) and, while its 2020 system stands, in Alaska.
Georgia's majority/runoff rule does not apply to presidential electors (O.C.G.A. § 21-2-501: 'no slate of candidates shall be required to receive a majority').
